resolved_age_model_config._paths_comment: Grid54 paths expand from /work/07980/bwa386/ls6/houfin/processed (TACC /work/07980/bwa386/ls6/houfin/processed; locally the same string via the ~/houfin/work symlink, grid54 itself a symlink to E:).
resolved_age_model_config._disease_arrival_map_comment: Per-pixel first-affected-breeding-season for House Finch mycoplasmal conjunctivitis, on the model grid. Built by scripts/build_disease_arrival_map.py from the documented 1994-2006 spread history (there is no published raster). Consumed by model_inputs.py as the onset gate for the K depression -- see src/model/age_fields.py.

kernel_contract._comment: The encoder supplies an uncentered 64-D Nyström feature map; model ingestion explicitly retains the first latent_dim (24) eigenfeatures to fit VRAM. Conditional on each w_scale, iid coefficients over those retained features imply Cov[H(x),H(x')|w_scale] = w_scale^2 Z_r(x)·Z_r(x'), the configured rank-r approximation to the original Ružička kernel. Truncation must be config-driven and recorded, never silent.

dispersal._comment: Single source of truth shared by Z_disp preparation and the forward model; resolved in exactly one place, build_kernels.dispersal_spec. Do not duplicate these boundaries in code.
dispersal._radial_splits_comment: juvenile_radial_splits_km takes either an explicit list of km boundaries (start 0.0, end >=1e8) or the string "derive" for equal-mass radial bands. The pinned literals are NOT quantiles of the current kernel. See docs/PRIORS.md#radial-splits.
dispersal._kernel_source_comment: Veit & Lewis 1996 kernels: the adult and juvenile SHAPES DIFFER (0.859 vs 0.468). See docs/PRIORS.md#dispersal-kernels.
dispersal._path_comment: Z_disp is intentionally a land-conditioned neighborhood/path summary: at each fractional displacement, water/nodata is excluded and the remaining land contribution is normalized. It is not a literal trajectory hazard through water.
dispersal._kernel_discretization_comment: Resolved by dispersal_spec.kernel_discretization, NOT part of dispersal_spec's dict (existing path metadata unchanged). cell_integrated = the PDF averaged over the source-uniform x destination-uniform cell displacement (31x31 midpoint rule per axis pair); used for the forward kernels AND Z_disp. Point sampling at 54 km would put 0.237 of adult mass on the self-cell vs 0.123 integrated.

age_structure_prior._comment: Resolution-invariant weak local-age-structure regularizer. We average log Beta density over land cell-years, then multiply by effective_sites, instead of treating every grid cell/year as an independent prior observation. This is a distributional belief about a representative local cell, not a prior on the domain-wide mean.

population_model._comment: Mechanistic/data-scale constants persisted into model-input metadata; no hidden grid or invasion constants in ingestion code.
population_model._scale_comment: THE GAUGE: population_scale_route_counts_per_relative_unit converts model density to the mean of a BBS route count. A sampler-conditioning choice, not biology -- the likelihood is invariant to it. See docs/PRIORS.md#the-gauge.
population_model._release_allee_comment: Years from the release (invasion_timestep) during which the 9 candidate release cells skip the mate-finding Allee factor. The Allee term models continental colonization (thin arrivals into a 27 km cell); released cage birds were aggregated far below grid scale, so mates did not limit them. Without this the fit inflated and concentrated the founder pulse to clear the cell-averaged threshold -- a saddle with corner-shaped modes (probe of run_17). Matches invasion_window_years. 0 restores the old behaviour.
population_model._dispersal_random_comment: Per-year Normal(0, 0.001) noise on the dispersal logit. At that scale it moves dispersal by ~0.025%; the run_18 probe found its 124 directions exactly at prior curvature and L-BFGS moved it ~3e-5. false removes the site (the model uses zeros). See docs/PRIORS.md#structural-switches.
population_model._disease_prior_comment: The mycoplasmal-conjunctivitis effect on capacity, as a STRUCTURED hypothesis: K = K_base * (1 - severity(x) * onset_gate(x,t) * (1 - recovery(t - arrival))). See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-term and src/model/age_fields.py.
population_model._capacity_level_comment: Prior on K's continental LEVEL, in expected BBS route counts, anchored on the typical OCCUPIED cell (median 2.618). See docs/PRIORS.md#capacity-level.
population_model._allee_comment: Allee half-saturation on the BBS ROUTE-COUNT scale: allee_factor = 1 - 2^(-C/n50), half released at C = n50. See docs/PRIORS.md#allee-effect.
population_model._initpop_comment: The t=0 (1902) native-range seed, as a FRACTION OF LOCAL FITTED CAPACITY rather than an absolute abundance. Read the consequence of core_fraction_of_local_capacity = 1.0 before changing it. See docs/PRIORS.md#initial-population.
population_model._invasion_pulse_comment: The 1940 release, as a fraction of a FIXED, empirically observed, K-independent reference -- deliberately not tied to k_level or local K_base. See docs/PRIORS.md#invasion-pulse.
population_model._invasion_sites_comment: invasion_sites = 9: the record documents one known sighting, not that it was the only release, and at 27 km the literal coordinate may not land on a valid cell. See docs/PRIORS.md#invasion-sites.
population_model._invasion_budget_comment: With 90 free (site, year) coefficients the SHARED prior must tighten, or the term becomes a high-dimensional escape hatch. See docs/PRIORS.md#invasion-budget.

capacity_level_prior._link_switch_comment: softplus (default) or exp. At the operating point the softplus argument is ~-2.1, where softplus ~ exp, so low K costs the same under both; exp removes softplus's shrinkage of the upper tail. alpha_k's location is re-solved per link so the level median stays at target_level_median_route_counts. See docs/PRIORS.md#structural-switches.
capacity_level_prior._link_comment: K uses a SOFTPLUS link applied in DENSITY space: K = softplus(alpha_k + gamma_k*H_k + trend), no gauge conversion around it. See docs/PRIORS.md#capacity-link.
capacity_level_prior._calibration_comment: target_level_median_route_counts is the belief; alpha_k's prior LOCATION is solved from it at import by age_priors._softplus_loc_for_median. See docs/PRIORS.md#capacity-calibration.

population_model._manifold_comment: Correlated weights for FOUR demographic manifolds, ordered [survival_adult, reproduction, capacity, survival_juv] -- survival_juv is APPENDED, so w_env[:,0..2] keeps its meaning for positional readers. See docs/PRIORS.md#manifold-prior.
population_model._amplitude_comment: GP AMPLITUDE, one per manifold: w_scale_j = softplus(Normal(amplitude_loc_j, amplitude_scale_j)), so Var(beta_j) = w_scale_j^2 and H_j is a GP conditional on it. See docs/PRIORS.md#gp-amplitude.

manifold_prior._form_comment: rank2 (two coupled groups via communality + angle, below) or exchangeable (ONE coupling rho for all four fields: beta_j = w_scale_j*(sqrt(rho)*f + sqrt(1-rho)*eps_j); rho = sigmoid(Normal(logit(coupling_target), coupling_logit_scale))). See docs/PRIORS.md#structural-switches.
manifold_prior._capdem_comment: LEVER E (subagent proposal): K may depart from the shared demographic habitat direction; corr ~ logit-normal(.85, .15)

population_model._k_range_comment: REPORTING threshold only -- not an active constraint. K is softplus(alpha_k + gamma_k*H_k + trend) with nothing bounding it below, so a collapse is meant to be VISIBLE in metrics.json:k_range rather than hidden by a clamp. 24x is +/-2 log SD of the observed occupied-cell spread (log sd 1.592, from scripts/diagnostics/bbs_abundance_quantiles.py), i.e. the fold range the data actually show; a realized range well beyond it means K is being used to explain absence that should be explained by lambda < 1.
population_model._k_trend_comment: Continental smooth time trend on K's pre-softplus argument, time-centered so alpha_k keeps the level. A SAFETY VALVE AND FAILURE DIAGNOSTIC, not a modeled mechanism. See docs/PRIORS.md#k-trend.

disease_prior._severity_comment: DENSITY-DEPENDENT severity: a Hill function of local carrying capacity, because epidemics need hosts. See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-severity.
disease_prior._ceiling_comment: severity_ceiling is now LOAD-BEARING FOR IDENTIFIABILITY, not merely a bound on plausibility. K = K_base*(1 - severity(K_base)*...) must be monotone in K_base, or two different habitat qualities map to the same realized capacity. At 0.5 monotonicity holds for every n tested (min dK/dK_base = 0.100 at n=5); at 0.7 it BREAKS (slope -0.26). It also happens to match the documented ~50-60% decline, which was measured in the dense eastern populations -- exactly where this parameterization applies it. Do not raise it above ~0.6 without re-checking monotonicity.
disease_prior._mu_comment: Logit of the MODIFIER on density-dependent severity, not of the removed fraction itself: severity = severity_ceiling * sigmoid(mu + ...) * hill(K_base). See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-severity-modifier.
disease_prior._field_comment: sev_field_budget is the total regional deviation the severity field may add on the logit scale (distributed as budget/sqrt(n) per coefficient); 0.5 comfortably reaches west ~25-30% vs east ~60%. lag0_scale/lag_field_budget are YEARS of onset-timing slack, continental and regional respectively -- the arrival map is a hand-built smoothed reconstruction, so its timing is coarse both overall and regionally.
disease_prior._late_comment: Severity coefficient on decades since the EPIDEMIC'S OWN start (disease_start_year=1993), not since any cell's local arrival. See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-late-era.
disease_prior._native_comment: NATIVE-LINEAGE severity suppression, on the same dimensionless core/margin shape that seeds 1902 abundance. See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-native-resistance.
disease_prior._recovery_comment: Slowly increasing resilience after local arrival: the hit decays toward severity*(1-recovery_fraction) with an e-folding time of recovery_tau years. recovery_logit_loc=-0.5 -> prior median ~38% of the hit eventually recovered, spanning 0 to ~90%.

observation_mask._pinned_comment: holdout_blocks.pinned_blocks (fit code GRID54_LADDER ac521d8): withhold exactly the 31 216-km blocks the 27 km s64 fit withheld (written by research/exp/grid54_pin_holdout.py from that fit's draw); block_cells 4 x 54 km = 216 km, fraction/seed ignored.

retention_overflow.capacity_census: pre-departure total A+J; inherited K units

map._comment: Continuation begins under tight priors and progressively relaxes them at absolute optimizer steps. The standard/full run uses 300 tight + 300 intermediate + 1200 nominal-prior steps (1800 total). Boundaries are independent of TOTAL_STEPS so extending/resuming a run cannot move backward. lr_decay_steps is likewise fixed across extensions; after step 900 optimization continues at the schedule's minimum learning rate.
map._log_every_comment: Steps between '[map] step ...' progress lines on stdout (the SLURM .o log). tqdm also carries the loss, but it writes a single carriage-return-rewritten line to stderr, so a running fit's loss trajectory is otherwise invisible in the log. Override per-run with HOUFIN_MAP_LOG_EVERY; 0 disables. A profile may set its own value.

quick90._comment: Short development fit: 100 tight, 100 intermediate and 200 nominal-prior steps (400 total, per prior_relaxation below). The learning-rate decay reaches its minimum at step 300 (lr_decay_steps) and stays there for the final 100. This changes optimization only, not the final MAP objective. The name is historical -- it was a 900-step, ~90-minute profile before the schedule was compressed; it is now much shorter.

runtime._comment: Production JAX jobs require a GPU and explicitly place model inputs in VRAM. HOUFIN_MODEL_INPUT_RESIDENCY=host is experimental: lax.scan is not a true differentiable host-streaming mechanism. SLURM wrappers record nvidia-smi VRAM/utilization plus host MemAvailable/SwapFree every 30 seconds (the interval is the second positional argument to start_gpu_monitor in the .slurm files, not a config key).

resolved_age_model_config._comment: Round1 clean seeds1/2: one shared space-for-time coefficient field; absolute aggregated Allee unchanged.
resolved_age_model_config._grid54_comment: 54 km resolution diagnostic (research/experiments/GRID54_INPUTS_2026-10-29.md): a mirror of the shared-readout summer64 fit's resolved config (research/FINAL_SHARED_ROUND1_20261025/s64/resolved_config.json) with 54 km paths and the grid-dependent values re-derived. The gauge (20) is unchanged (54 km q95 17.3).

pseudo_zero_subsample._comment: Read by src/data/combine/model_inputs.py: keep exactly n_sites pre-invasion pseudo-zero sites (x 38 years) instead of the real-data-density rule, so the 54 km input carries the 27 km s64 input's absence OBSERVATION count (1814 x 38 = 68,932). Decision 2026-10-29 (coordinator).

resolved_age_model_config._grid54_step1_comment: GRID54 ladder step 1: step 0 + RELATIVE Allee (mate-finding by N/K), n50/K pinned at .0197 (V&L-derived ratio, as E071c/55e; n50_raw = softplus^-1(.0197)); aggregation_k 3 kept.
resolved_age_model_config._grid54_step2_comment: Step 2 (GRID54_LADDER_2026-10-29.md): step 1 + single habitat field, manifold_prior.fixed_coupling 1.0 (beta_j = w_scale_j * f: every rate, capacity included, reads H = Z.f with its own positive amplitude; no private parts).
resolved_age_model_config._grid54_step3_comment: Step 3 (GRID54_LADDER_2026-10-29.md): step 2 + observer x route effect (sigma_u 0.97 fixed, eta ~ N(0,1)) on the obsroute input; fit code b66f51a.

resolved_data_config._paths_comment: All paths are portable: /home/breallis/houfin/scratch/houfin/data (raw + processed 27 km products) and /work/07980/bwa386/ls6/houfin/processed (model inputs/results) expand at load time (src/config_utils.py). They default to <repo>/data and <repo>/data/processed for local dev; on HPC export HOUFIN_DATA/HOUFIN_PROCESSED.

trends._comment: Gridded trend products aligned to the model grid by preprocess/bbs_trend.py and preprocess/ebird_trend.py (both keyed to community_trend_list). BBS: long-term %/yr per cell (nearest clip/pad, zero resampling -- ref grid is on the BBS lattice). eBird: abd_ppy (%/yr) + abd (mid-window rel. abundance) per cell, centroids projected from WGS84 and binned. Consumed by community_encoder/train_DESK/trend_community.py.

resolved_data_config._ebird_trends_comment: eBird Status & Trends 'trends' product, fetched from the SAME REST API + key as the weekly abundance (acquire/ebird.py --trends), NOT the ebirdst R package. Trends live under version year 2022 (2023 has none); objkey {year}/{sp}/trends/{sp}_{season}_ebird-trends_{year}.parquet, the season token discovered per-species from the listing. Tabular (one row per 27 km cell): abd_ppy (%/yr trend), abd_trend (cumulative %), abd (mid-window relative abundance), WGS84 lon/lat centroids, window 2012-2022.
resolved_data_config._community_trend_comment: Written by identify/select_trend_community.py: the union of four per-axis top-N cuts (bbs.community_axes) over the species present in BOTH trend products (BBS tr{AOU}.tif AND eBird has-trends), House Finch excluded. Columns species_code, aou, season, sci_norm, mean_rank, category, migration. mean_rank is a SYNTHESIZED round-robin order over the union (a union has no natural total order, but three readers sort on this column); category records which axes chose each species, and migration is the AVONET class 1/2/3. Drives the trend downloads + the trend->annual community cube. Differs from the weekly community.
resolved_data_config._focal_comment: The transfer TARGET of the downstream statistical model. avonet.py already excludes it from reference_community_ranked.csv; this is the defense-in-depth code that the eBird selection + BBS crosswalk also filter, so a stale ranked list can never leak House Finch into the community Z.

timeline._comment: Single source of truth for the model timeline (see src/temporal.py, docs/TEMPORAL.md). Model year T = climate bio-year Aug(T-1)->Jul(T), aligned to the ~June BBS count. first_year=1902 (first FULL bio-year, since climate obs start Jan 1901); end_year=2025 (newest BBS: 2026 release, 1966-2025 field seasons); invasion_year=1940 (NYC release; inv_timestep is DERIVED as invasion_year-first_year, never hardcoded); disease_start_year=1993 (winter the mycoplasmal-conjunctivitis epizootic began in the mid-Atlantic; disease_timestep is likewise DERIVED, and bounds the K-depression term in src/model/age_fields.py); bbs_start_year=1966 (first BBS field season -- the model runs from 1902 but has zero observational constraint before this year; used as a visualization reference line, never to gate/trim the model timeline itself). Land use/soil use the calendar-year-T state; only climate uses the bio-year window. Lagging covariates (e.g. LUH-3 ends 2024) are EMA-carried to end_year.

grid._box_comment: Fixed study-area extent (left, bottom, right, top) in box_crs = USA Contiguous Albers NAD83 (ESRI:102003), the native CRS of the USGS BBS mapping rasters (trend/abundance, 27 km). The box is the lon/lat region [-125..-66, 24..53] (CONUS + southern Canada; AK, far-northern Canada and most of Mexico clipped out) reprojected to 102003, with its ORIGIN SNAPPED to the BBS 27 km lattice (residues x=20068.8961, y=15815.4047 mod 27000) so BBS trend rasters land on this grid with ZERO resampling (clip/pad only). 133 rows x 224 cols at 27 km. build_ref_grid defaults to these when given no --base-raster/--bounds, so the canonical ref grid builds standalone on any machine.
grid._comment: Single source of truth for the model grid. target_res_m is THE model resolution (27 km), matching the native resolution of the trend products this pipeline targets (USGS BBS mapping rasters, 27 km ESRI:102003; eBird Status & Trends, 27 km). Continental products (climate/climr, LUH-3, HYDE, SoilGrids, DEM, eBird abundance) are aggregated onto ref_raster via regrid.reproject_to_ref `average`; the BBS trend rasters share this CRS+lattice and align by nearest clip/pad (no resampling of the ground truth). Nonlinear steps (Ruzicka kernel/PCA for Z, quantiles, transforms) are applied at this resolution -- Z is built at 27 km, never pooled. The prior 25 km ESRI:102039 CONUS box and the older 16 km / 4 km BUI-grid pipeline both live in git history; BUI now ingests onto THIS lattice via src/data/preprocess/bui.py.

regions._comment: Named region rasters on the model grid, built by scripts and consumed by diagnostics. great_plains_zones is the gap-free west|barrier|east corridor partition (codes 1/2/3, nodata 0) written by scripts/build_great_plains_mask.py from the EPA/CEC Ecoregions Level I shapefile. The shapefile is NOT in git (/data/ is gitignored) and is not in download_all.sh, so the raster must be built where the vector lives and scp'd to HPC; consumers skip cleanly when it is absent. This key lives in data_config.json rather than age_model_config.json on purpose: the MAP fingerprint hashes the entire resolved age-model config, so adding a key there would invalidate resume of every existing checkpoint.

coastline._comment: Terrestrial model mask (src/data/preprocess/land_mask.py). Natural Earth 10m polygonal lakes are subtracted from continental land on a fine grid before aggregation, so Great Lakes are water while narrow rivers are never expanded. The configured study exclusions deliberately encode Cuba/Bahamas as off-domain water for this model; Mexico is not excluded here. The terrestrial fraction is thresholded at land_fraction_tau (>=tau => model land).

avonet._comment: Reference-community identification inputs, all auto-fetched by acquire/avonet.py. AVONET traits + BirdLife/BirdTree crosswalk + precomputed Hackett MCC phylogeny (.nex) from figshare ELEData.zip (found by name via the figshare v2 API) -> {datasets_root}/avonet. eBird taxonomy from the eBird API (ref/taxonomy/ebird, no key; the Cornell web CSV is Cloudflare-walled). Urban-tolerance indices from a separate public figshare article -> {datasets_root}/urban_avian.

dem._comment: Global DEM for the climate elevation-quantile step (preprocess/elevation.py -> climr). Default: NOAA NCEI ETOPO 2022 60-arc-second (~1.85 km) surface elevation, a single global GeoTIFF over public HTTPS (no auth). Swap `url` for a finer DEM (e.g. GMTED2010 7.5-arc-second) if desired; elevation.py is source-agnostic.

elevation._comment: preprocess/elevation.py reprojects the DEM onto a sub-grid fine_factor x finer than the model grid, then takes per-cell p10/p50/p90 elevation. fine_factor should be >= target_res/DEM_native so no DEM detail is lost (27 km / ~1.85 km ETOPO ~= 14.6 -> 15).

climate._comment: climr downscaling. mode 'subgrid' (default): a grid x grid mesh of true-elevation sub-points per cell -> real spatial+elevation quantiles (captures horizontal gradients). mode 'elev_quantile': centroid at three elevation quantiles (elevation-only, cheaper). obs_ts_dataset feeds the annual observed series; obs year range clamps to climr's extent.

resolved_data_config._dataverse_comment: Harvard Dataverse (src/data/acquire/dataverse.py). The bui DOI is the DATASET that actually serves the files and is the one to keep; BUI_README.txt inside the download cites doi:10.7910/DVN/1WB9E4, which is the citation DOI for the broader 'Gridded Settlement Data for the Conterminous United States Over 200 years' deposit. They are not interchangeable -- do not 'correct' the one below to match the README.
resolved_data_config._bui_comment: HISDAC-US built-up intensity -> model grid (src/data/preprocess/bui.py). Source is 250 m EPSG:5070 (== ESRI:102039) float64 indoor building area in square feet, 43 snapshots at exactly 5-year spacing 1810-2020, CONTERMINOUS US ONLY; nodata is unset, so the rasters cover a rectangle and every cell outside CONUS reads 0.0. fine_factor is the sub-cell subdivision of the ref grid used before per-cell quantiling: 108 would nest 250 m exactly but costs a ~2.8 GB float64 intermediate per year, and 27 (~1 km, 729 samples per model cell) is ample for a quantile at 16x less memory. transform must stay non-null and invertible -- preprocess/bui.py needs it to compute the constant fill for cells outside the CONUS footprint, and it must match the bui stream's transform in esk_desk_config.json or the fill will not land at the in-coverage mean. The CONUS footprint itself comes from coastline.study_exclusion_source, read as an inclusion, because BUI encodes absence as 0 rather than nodata and so cannot report its own extent.

luh3._comment: LUH-3 v1.2 CMIP7 Historical (850-2024, 0.25deg). states + management only; transitions (17GB, flows not states) skipped.
luh3._exclude_comment: Uninformative management layers dropped from the covariate set: forest plantations (pltns, all-zero in LUH-3 V1), additional tree cover (addtc), 1st/2nd-generation biofuel crop fractions (cpbf1_*, cpbf2_*), plantation biofuel (pltns_bfuel), and wood-harvest carbon split (rndwd/fulwd/combf). All ~0 over North America.

hyde._comment: HYDE 3.5 baseline netCDF (5 arc-min global, one file per variable spanning all time points). Confirmed accessible over plain HTTP at geo.public.data.uu.nl (not the bot-protected public.yoda.uu.nl). Add urban_area.nc etc. to files if needed.

sciencebase._comment: USGS BBS releases via ScienceBase item file API. bbs = newest US/Canada release (2026 Release, 1966-2025). bbs_mexico = 2008-2018 UNPROCESSED (DOI 10.5066/P9L4KBDC); lacks RunType/RPID, incorporated with a quality covariate.

bbs_mexico._comment: whole_item (archive), NOT per-file: the per-file downloadUri for SpeciesData.csv 404s, which exits nonzero and would abort download_all.sh, while the whole-item archive downloads cleanly. SpeciesData.csv shipped as 0 bytes through mid-2026 and the ingest skipped Mexico non-fatally (bbs.load_mexico_observations returns None when it is missing or empty); it now downloads correctly, so Mexico rows enter as quality_tier 1. NOTE what that switches on: obs_quality is no longer constant, so the NB2 quality down-weighting in age_priors (guarded on max(obs_quality) > min(obs_quality)) begins sampling quality_conc_mult -- the model gains a parameter, and MAP results and the run fingerprint change accordingly.

bbs_trends._comment: USGS BBS Mapping products 1966-2022 (DOI 10.5066/P1DPJPSI): per-species trend rasters tr{AOU}.tif = long-term geometric-mean %/yr population change 1966-2022, 27 km ESRI:102003 (NAD83 Albers), 516 species, 5-digit AOU code in the filename. Run download with --extract to unpack tr*.tif.

bbs_abundance._comment: Same ScienceBase item as bbs_trends: the ABUNDANCE rasters ra{AOU}.tif = 2018-2022 mean relative abundance (birds/route), 27 km ESRI:102003, 520 species. Used ONLY as the method-B deep-reconstruction scale (trend_community: deep past = k*B/f, k=median(eBird/BBS present)), NOT as community abundance values. Run download with --extract to unpack ra*.tif.

resolved_data_config._comment: 54 km resolution diagnostic data config (see config/overlays/grid54_age.json and research/experiments/GRID54_INPUTS_2026-10-29.md). Same box/origin as 27 km; 67 x 112 cells with one virtual all-ocean row padded at the south.
